## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Duddadajātaka* (Ja 180) is the tenth story of the *Kalyāṇadhammavagga* in the Jātaka collection [Fausböll 1879]. The narrative opens with the verse incipit *Duddadaṃ dadamānānaṃ* ("Tis hard to do as good men do") [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879]. Set at Jetavana, the story of the present relates an occasion when two friendly householders in Sāvatthī collected subscriptions to sponsor a seven-day communal almsgiving (*gaṇadāna*) of all requisites to the monastic Saṅgha headed by the Buddha [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879]. In the story of the past, the Bodhisatta is identified as the leader of a band of ascetics (*gaṇasatthā*), while his ascetic followers are identified as the Buddha's contemporary assembly (*buddhaparisā*) [Fausböll 1879]. Four modern translations in four languages are recorded on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

Passage-level parallels curated by SuttaCentral include the *Maccharisutta* (SN 1.32), the *Bilārakosiyajātaka* (Ja 450), and the *Vessantarajātaka* (Ja 547) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus independently detects Pali-internal text reuse aligning directly with SuttaCentral's parallels, identifying matches between the verses of Ja 180 (§§0.4–2.4 and 1.1–2.4) and both the *Bilārakosiyajātaka* (§§4.4–6.4) and the *Vessantarajātaka* (§§643.1–644.4) with high similarity scores [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral]. No cross-language matches of significant score are reported in DharmaNexus [DharmaNexus].
